facts: The book's core promise, in its publisher blurb: quiet the mind, feel less stressed and less tired in just ten minutes a day.
The exercise is called Take10: ten minutes, once a day, with the steps of sitting upright, a few deep breaths, then natural breathing, and returning to the breath when the mind wanders.

Puddicombe left his sports science studies in 1994 after a bereavement and trained about ten years as a Buddhist monk in Nepal, India, Myanmar, Thailand, Russia and elsewhere, with full ordination in the Tibetan tradition at a Himalayan monastery in India; he returned to the UK in 2004.
Headspace was co-founded by Puddicombe and Richard Pierson in London in 2010, first as an events company; an app existed by January 2012.
Phrases attributed to the book: 'we are still only talking about ten minutes' and 'this is ten minutes that is going to set up your entire day for you'.
The ten minutes are described as a training ground for the rest of the waking day; the book carries mindfulness into eating, walking, running and falling asleep.
The book's author bio describes him as a former Buddhist monk with a degree in Circus Arts.

tension: A man who trained for about ten years in monasteries sells the practice as ten minutes a day.
opening_idea: Open on the contrast: about ten years of monastic training on one side, a method sized at ten minutes on the other.

lessons.idea: A practice sized to fit a day gets done; one sized to an ideal waits for a free afternoon that does not come.
lessons.anchor: The decision to size the method at ten minutes a day after years in monasteries.
lessons.example: Someone who wants to learn an instrument sets a short fixed slot after dinner instead of waiting for a free weekend.

reflect_final: Where in your usual day could a fixed ten minutes go without anything else being moved, and what is the practice you would put in it?

use_cases.situation: A friend says they have no time to start meditating.
use_cases.move: Mention that the book is built around ten minutes a day, one fixed slot, and ask where that slot could sit.

use_cases.situation: You want to begin a new habit.
use_cases.move: Size it to ten minutes and attach it to something you already do each day.

use_cases.situation: A team wants a wellbeing plan.
use_cases.move: Propose one ten-minute slot a day, as in the Take10 idea, before anything bigger.

pocket_idea: After years of monastic training, Puddicombe sized his method at ten minutes a day: pick a slot that fits your real day.
